headline: Jasper National Park Entry and Miette Road Access
reservation: A valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily entry fee is required for all visitors to Jasper National Park. While the hot springs themselves operate on a first-come, first-served basis, nearby accommodations at Jasper or Pocahontas must be booked months in advance. Always verify the seasonal opening and closing dates for the Miette Road, which is typically restricted during winter months.

days.title: The Fiddle Valley Ascent

stops.name: Sulphur Skyline Trail
stops.detail: Begin this steep ascent early to reach the summit for 360-degree views of the Fiddle River Valley before the afternoon heat.

stops.name: Miette Hot Springs
stops.detail: Relax in the hottest mineral springs in the Canadian Rockies after your hike, utilizing the varied temperature pools.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from Jasper; the Miette Road is winding with frequent wildlife sightings.
days.note: The hot springs can reach capacity mid-day; arriving immediately after a hike is a common strategy.

days.title: Ashman and Athabasca Confluence

stops.name: Punchbowl Falls
stops.detail: View the unique limestone mountain formations where the water has carved a distinct bowl shape near the Miette Road entrance.

stops.name: Jasper House National Historic Site
stops.detail: Walk the short trail to the viewpoint overlooking the site of a 19th-century fur trade post on the banks of the Athabasca River.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; stop at the various pullouts for bighorn sheep viewing.
days.note: Maintain a safe distance from wildlife; bighorn sheep are frequently found licking salt on the roadway.

days.title: Lakeside Reflection and History

stops.name: Talbot Lake
stops.detail: Stop at the rocky shoreline for birdwatching and views of the surrounding peaks reflected in the shallow waters.

stops.name: Pocahontas Mine Trail
stops.detail: Follow the interpretive loop through the ruins of a historic coal mining townsite located at the base of the Miette Road.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions are generally paved but subject to seasonal frost heaves.
days.note: Talbot Lake is shallow and prone to high winds; use caution if approaching the water's edge.

intel.title: Miette Terminal Parking
intel.text: The parking lot at the hot springs also serves the Sulphur Skyline trailhead and can fill by late morning. Overflow parking is available but adds walking distance to the facility entrance.

intel.title: Fiddle Valley Dead Zone
intel.text: Expect total loss of cellular signal once you turn onto Miette Road from Highway 16. Emergency payphones are available at the hot springs facility, but do not rely on digital navigation.

intel.title: Hinton vs Jasper
intel.text: There are no fueling stations on Miette Road. Hinton offers the most competitive prices before entering the park, while Jasper serves as the primary hub for western arrivals.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closure
intel.text: The road to Miette Hot Springs typically opens in May and closes in mid-October. Heavy snowfall can result in temporary closures outside of these months; verify status via Jasper National Park bulletins.

intel.title: Pool Entry Protocols
intel.text: Entry to the pools is managed on-site; during peak summer weekends, a waitlist system may be implemented. Towel and suit rentals are generally available but subject to facility supply.

plan.arrival: Arrive from Edmonton via Highway 16, stopping in Hinton for final groceries before entering the park gates at Pocahontas.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for the paved Miette Road; larger RVs should use caution on the tight switchbacks near the hot springs.
plan.goldenHour: The Ashman Ridge viewpoint on Miette Road provides excellent evening light across the Fiddle Range during the summer solstice.
